guard: A restore holds the chat stream at the recorded count and no age through every check of the restored state, then sets the age the backup recorded on the target and reads it back; a `cotal up` that fails after moving the chat stream's limit says so in its error and envelope.
command: pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/core build && pnpm --filter @cotal-ai/cli build && pnpm smoke:chat-history-restore:live
why: The suite drives `tsx bin/cotal.ts`, which loads core and the CLI from their built dist, so each mutation
rebuilds both and `afterRestore` rebuilds them from the restored source. The first scenario's posts are older
than the recorded age when the restore checks them, so a restore that set the age first would watch the broker
delete them during its own checks.

mutations.name: the restore stages the chat stream at the recorded age
mutations.expectRed: a restore whose posts are older than the recorded age passes its checks
mutations.cell: a restore whose posts are older than the recorded age passes its checks

mutations.name: the restore never sets the recorded age
mutations.find: if (chatRecord && wanted.includes(chatRecord.stream)) await applyRecordedChatAge(broker, journal.space, chatRecord);
mutations.expectRed: ...then holds the recorded age and count
mutations.cell: ...then holds the recorded age and count

mutations.name: a start that fails after the move does not say the limit moved
mutations.expectRed: a start that moves the limit and then fails on a later step says the limit moved
mutations.cell: a start that moves the limit and then fails on a later step says the limit moved
mutations.note: The broker deleted the posts older than the new age at the move, and the next start finds nothing to move, so this error is the only report of it.
